gaps.sentence: ___ books you left on my desk were really useful.
gaps.explanation: 'The books you left…' — the clause identifies which books.

gaps.sentence: They're building ___ new library near the town hall.
gaps.explanation: A new library — first mention; the town hall is the known one.

gaps.sentence: They sailed across ___ Mediterranean last summer.
gaps.explanation: Seas and oceans take 'the': the Mediterranean.
'The capital of Italy' — the of-phrase makes it unique and definite.

gaps.sentence: This is ___ second time you've been late this week.
He behaves as if he were ___ owner of the company.
gaps.explanation: 'The owner' — there is one owner, so 'the'.

gaps.sentence: She works as ___ editor for a travel magazine.
___ Lake Constance lies between Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
gaps.explanation: Lakes take no article when 'Lake' comes first.
